title: Training Periodization, Intensity Distribution, and Volume in Trained Cyclists: A Systematic Review
publisher: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
claims: Seven studies with 161 trained road cyclists met the inclusion criteria.

Block periodization used highly concentrated workload phases ranging from 1- to 8-week blocks, with training volume of 8.75–11.68 hours per week and both pyramidal and polarized intensity distributions.

Traditional periodization was characterized by a first period of high-volume/low-intensity training before reducing volume and increasing the proportion of high-intensity training; volume ranged from 7.5 to 10.76 hours per week and a pyramidal distribution was used.
The authors concluded that no evidence is currently available favoring a specific periodization model during 8 to 12 weeks in trained road cyclists.
Few studies have examined the seasonal impact of different periodization models in a systematic way.
